act.label: Lov
act.note: Danish § (Paragraf) maps to AKN article, following civil law convention. Higher divisions (Kapitel, Afsnit) used only in larger acts. Short acts may have no higher divisions at all.

lovbekendtgorelse.label: Lovbekendtgørelse
lovbekendtgorelse.note: Consolidated text (lovbekendtgørelse) supersedes the original act as citation authority. Same structure as act. Model as a separate FRBR work with activeModifications linking to original. URI uses the bekendtgørelse number and year.

bekendtgorelse.label: Bekendtgørelse
bekendtgorelse.note: Executive order (secondary legislation) issued by ministry under statutory authority. Often more detailed than the parent lov. Separate FRBR work. URI prefix bkg.

grundloven.label: Danmarks Riges Grundlov
grundloven.note: The Constitution (1953). No Afsnit or Kapitel — only §§ grouped loosely by thematic clusters without formal structural markers. §§ numbered 1–89.

numbering.insertion_note: Inserted §§ use a space before the letter suffix: § 5 a, § 5 b. eId omits the space: art_5a, art_5b.

enacting_formulae.text: Bekendtgøres herved, at Folketinget har vedtaget følgende lov:
enacting_formulae.note: This formula appears in the Lovtidende publication notice, not within the act body itself.

enacting_formulae.text: I medfør af § {N} i lov om {X}, jf. lovbekendtgørelse nr. {NNN} af {dato}, fastsættes:
enacting_formulae.note: Enabling formula for executive orders, citing the parent lov provision.

amendments.phrasing: I [lov], foretages følgende ændringer: ... affattes således: ...
amendments.note: Amending acts (ændringslove) use the Artikellov format: each article of the amending act targets a specific existing act. Individual changes within each article are numbered 1., 2., 3. etc.

structuring.prompt_additions: Danish § (Paragraf) maps to ARTICLE keyword and AKN article element. Kapitel (Chapter) maps to CHAPTER. Afsnit (Part/Section) maps to PART. Stykke (stk.) maps to PARAGRAPH — the first stykke is stk. 1 marked inline as 'Stk. 1.' not in parentheses. Nummer (nr.) maps to POINT, numbered 1), 2). Litra maps to INDENT, lettered a), b). The § symbol is part of the number display but should not be included in the ARTICLE number field in Bluebell input. Many short Danish acts have no Kapitel — just a sequence of ARTICLEs. The final ARTICLE is always the commencement provision (ikrafttrædelsesbestemmelse).

supranational_memberships.note: Denmark has two EU opt-outs in force as of 2026: (1) Economic and Monetary Union stage 3 — Denmark retains the krone and is not part of the euro area (Edinburgh Agreement 1992, Protocol 16 TFEU); (2) Area of Freedom, Security and Justice — Denmark does not participate in EU decisions on justice and home affairs, with a limited opt-in mechanism since 2015 (Protocol 22 TFEU). A third opt-out — Common Security and Defence Policy — was abolished by the 1 June 2022 referendum (effective 1 July 2022), so CSDP is NOT in the current excluded_subjects list. Citizenship of the Union opt-out has been functionally lapsed since the Treaty of Amsterdam.
protocol_references: Protocol 22 TFEU (Area of Freedom, Security and Justice)
Protocol 16 TFEU (on certain provisions relating to Denmark)

supranational_memberships.note: ECHR incorporated via European Convention Act (lov nr. 285 af 1992).

territorial_scope.note: Most acts explicitly state in a final § whether they apply to Greenland and/or the Faroe Islands. Default is exclusion unless the § states otherwise. Greenland and Faroe Islands have separate legal systems and require separate jurisdiction profiles (gl, fo).

validation.note: Public reference profile; synthetic XML controls do not certify corpus coverage.
